TL;DR


## Key takeaways


1. A USD account and local-currency accounts should share one ledger and one review process.
2. International accounts can receive USD over SWIFT, plus EUR, GBP, AED, BRL, and MXN.
3. Bank partners issue and hold the accounts; Infinite runs onboarding, screening, and reconciliation.
4. Rail choice still depends on what the payer can send and what you need to hold.
5. Onboarding is assisted; currencies and flows are scoped with the team.


01


## Why hold both, rather than converting everything to dollars?


Many global businesses still need to collect and hold USD: US customers, dollar invoices, or dollar operating expenses. They also get paid, or need to pay, in other currencies. If every non-dollar payment is converted immediately, you take FX on arrival whether or not you needed dollars that day. If every dollar account lives in a separate bank from the local accounts, treasury reconstructs a position from two statements.


The useful pattern is both, on one ledger: a USD account for dollar activity, and international accounts for the currencies you actually receive or hold. Conversions become a decision, not a side effect of where the account lives.


02


## What does each account receive?


[USD bank accounts](https://infinite.net/accounts/usd) are the dollar account in the Infinite Accounts family.[International accounts](https://infinite.net/accounts/international) receive USD over SWIFT, and payments in EUR, GBP, AED, BRL, and MXN, each with its own account details for payers. Wallet accounts, where you need them, add stablecoin custody beside those balances.


The two are designed to sit together: international-account balances share the ledger with USD bank accounts and wallet accounts. You do not have to operate a second treasury system to accept euro or peso payments alongside dollars.


03


## How do onboarding and screening work when both exist?


Once, then continuously, for the customer that owns the accounts. Infinite runs KYC and KYB, sanctions screening, and monitoring for the business or for the customer you are opening accounts for. Adding a currency or an international account should not mean starting a second, unrelated review. The same program screens transfers before funds move, whichever account receives them.


Eligibility, documents, and corridor details are scoped during onboarding, which is assisted. This page does not restate application checklists or insurance language; those live on the account pages and in legal disclosures.


04


## How should treasury use the two together?


Collect in the currency you were paid in when you have a reason to hold it. Convert when you need USD, or when you need a local currency for a payout, not automatically on arrival.[FX](https://infinite.net/payments/fx) and[Transfer Routes](https://infinite.net/platform/transfer-routes) are the movement layer; the accounts are where the balances sit. Reconciliation should close from one ledger, so a dollar invoice and a euro inbound payment can be explained in the same report.


Coverage for where you can collect or pay is on the[coverage list](https://infinite.net/resources/coverage) . Do not infer a country list from the currencies an international account can receive.


FAQ


## Frequently asked questions


### Is a USD account the same thing as an international account?


No. A USD account is the dollar bank account. An international account receives USD over SWIFT plus EUR, GBP, AED, BRL, and MXN. On Infinite they share a ledger, but they are different account types with different account details for payers.


### Do you need a second bank relationship to collect local currencies?


Not on this model. Bank partners issue and hold both the USD and the international accounts, and Infinite runs onboarding, screening, and reconciliation so the balances sit together.


### Can a platform open both kinds of accounts for its customers?


Yes. International accounts are available for your business or for each customer, and they sit beside USD accounts on the same ledger. Onboarding and screening still run before accounts are used and before transfers move.
